title: Non-Hermitian topology driven by an identity term: An exactly solvable paradigm
authors: Lingfang Li, Yating Wei, Yang Ruan, Gangzhou Wu, Jun Wang, Shihua Chen, Tong Lin, Ching Hua Lee, Zhenhua Ni
abstract: An identity term in the Hamiltonian is conventionally regarded as spectrally inert-it shifts energies but does not alter eigenstate topology. We show that under non-Hermitian skin pumping, this paradigm fails: a momentum-dependent identity term actively deforms the generalized Brillouin zone, thereby challenging established topological criteria that rely on fixed complex contours. Here, by introducing spin-orbit coupling into a Hatano-Nelson chain, we present an exact analytical solution for the entire non-Hermitian eigensystem under open boundary conditions. Our solution reveals how inter-cell spin-orbit coupling, synergizing with this non-trivial identity term, induces topological edge states and robust zero modes in the complete absence of chiral symmetry. This work establishes an exactly solvable paradigm for non-Hermitian topology beyond symmetry protection, and provides a rigorous benchmark for testing topological invariants in systems with momentum-dependent identity terms.
summary: This paper develops an exactly solvable theoretical paradigm for non-Hermitian topology driven by momentum-dependent identity terms. By studying an SO-coupled Hatano-Nelson chain, the authors show that such terms actively deform the system's Brillouin Zone, leading to topological edge states and zero modes even when conventional symmetries are absent. This establishes a rigorous benchmark for testing topological invariants in complex open quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper challenges established topological criteria for non-Hermitian systems by showing that a momentum-dependent identity term can actively deform the Generalized Brillouin Zone (GBZ), invalidating fixed contour assumptions.
main_result: They establish an exactly solvable paradigm demonstrating that inter-cell spin-orbit coupling, combined with this identity term, induces robust topological edge states and zero modes even without chiral symmetry protection.
method: The authors provide exact analytical solutions for the non-Hermitian eigensystem under open boundary conditions by solving characteristic polynomial equations derived from the Hamiltonian structure.
model_or_system: The model is an SO-coupled 1D Hatano-Nelson (HN) chain, generalized to a fully generic two-band system. The Hamiltonian includes a momentum-dependent identity term $\epsilon_0(\mathbf{k})\mathbb{I}$ alongside spin-orbit coupling terms.
key_observables: Topological edge states, robust zero modes, and the deformation of the Generalized Brillouin Zone (GBZ).
important_parameters: Inter-cell SO coupling ($	ilde{t}_2$), identity term parameters ($\epsilon_0(\mathbf{k})$), and system size ($N$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on deriving exact analytical solutions for the OBC spectrum, extending beyond previous criteria that required fixed GBZ contours or specific symmetries.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the SO-coupled HN chain showing GBZ deformation and induced edge states. Phase diagrams map out topological regimes based on coupling strengths, confirming bulk-boundary correspondence via energy band analysis.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first introducing the physical model and identifying the failure point in standard topology theory. It then presents the exact analytical solution for the OBC spectrum using polynomial equations derived from the Hamiltonian. Finally, it analyzes the resulting topological phases and confirms robustness against disorder.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, generalizable framework for analyzing non-Hermitian systems where simple symmetry arguments fail due to complex momentum dependence in the identity term, which is crucial for understanding open quantum systems.
